rounds.summary: Seven acceptance criteria verified, no failure, one ledger finding: two go-test lines the implementer quoted for AC1 and AC3 came from the pre-simplify head's run rather than from the job they cited. Corrected in the pull request body at the architect's direction.

The reviewer's six minor findings folded in rather than deferred. Re-verified every criterion and drove the round's real change: the --check guard's GEN_GO_CHECK_ROOT redirect, and that running the gen-go tests no longer mutates the shared workspace's tracked generated files. One note: the controller skill's new report budget read `under about 2,000` while its live proof asserts a hard `<= 2000`.

Text only - no runtime code changed. The reviewer's important finding (and my round-2 note) is fixed: the controller skill now says `of at most 2,000 characters`, which agrees exactly with stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:5461's `<= 2000` and the README row's `within 2,000 characters`. The minor finding is fixed too: packages/contracts/AGENTS.md's generated-file registry now names both Go outputs, which matches what the generator writes.

proof.criterion: The reviewer's important finding, and my round-2 note: the controller daily report's instruction must not be softer than the live proof that measures it.
proof.surface: The three artefacts a controller and the Stage 4b run meet: the skill an agent loads, its compiled claude-envoy copy, and the live proof's own assertion and documentation.
proof.command: In this pod at this head: `grep -rn "about 2,000|under about" skills/ packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/ scripts/e2e/`; `grep -n "at most 2,000" skills/legion-controller/SKILL.md packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/legion-controller/SKILL.md`; `grep -n "length) <= 2000" scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh`; `grep -c "within 2,000 characters" scripts/e2e/README.md`; `wc -l` on both skill copies; `bun run check-dist` in packages/claude-envoy.
proof.observed: No soft wording survives anywhere in skills/, the compiled copies or scripts/e2e. Both skill copies read `of at most 2,000 characters` at line 341, the proof asserts `(.payload.body | length) <= 2000` at stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:5461, and README.md:1452 documents it as `within 2,000 characters`: instruction and measurement now agree exactly, so a controller that obeys the skill cannot fail that row for length. Both copies are 498 lines, under pi-legion's 500-line body guard, and `dist/ and legion/ match a fresh build`, so the compiled copy is a regeneration rather than a hand-edit.
proof.negativeControl: The defect this closes is its own control: at the previous head the same greps found `under about 2,000 characters` in both copies against the proof's hard `<= 2000`, which is what I reported in round 2. The compiled copy is controlled by check-dist, which in round 1 refused a hand-edited bundle with `generated files are stale (dist/dispatch.js)`.

proof.criterion: The reviewer's minor finding: the registry that tells an agent which files are generated must name every file the generator writes.
proof.surface: packages/contracts/AGENTS.md as an agent reads it, against packages/contracts/scripts/gen-go.ts as it runs, and against the guard that enforces the rule.
proof.command: Read `gen-go.ts:439-452` for the outputs list; read the AGENTS.md rows at :13-14, :23-25 and :114-115; then `bun run check:go` with a `// hand-edited` line appended to each tracked generated file in turn, restoring each.
proof.observed: The generator writes exactly two outputs (`packages/envoy/internal/contracts/generated.go`, `packages/daemon/internal/dispatch/generated.go`) and the registry now names both: the summary line, a table row of its own for the daemon output explaining why it exists (the daemon is a Go module whose production build imports nothing from the envoy module), the `--check` row rewritten to say it compares a fresh render of each and names the one it finds stale, and the hand-edit prohibition covering both. Every claim in those rows is true of the code at this head.
proof.negativeControl: The prohibition is backed, not just written: a hand-edit of `packages/daemon/internal/dispatch/generated.go` made `bun run check:go` exit 1 with `... /packages/daemon/internal/dispatch/generated.go is stale`, and the same of `packages/envoy/internal/contracts/generated.go` exited 1 naming that one. Both restored; the check exits 0 and `jj status` reports no change.

notes: Round 2's note is closed by this round and needs no further work: instruction and proof now say the same hard 2,000, verified word for word in all three artefacts.

Nothing in this round changes behaviour, so no acceptance criterion needed a new kind of evidence; what it needed was re-citation at the head that will merge, which is what the proof entries above carry.

The deploy skew remains measurable rather than theoretical: at this head the real `dispatch comment` sent a 32,000-unit body and the live INFRA Dispatch refused it `(32000/2000)`. Production carries the old cap, so the production check after the merge will meet a build without this change until Dispatch is deployed (dispatch://INFRA-64).

Three thermonuclear findings the reviewer examined and did not hold (the GEN_GO_CHECK_ROOT seam's shape, the `takes more once it is split` clause, and the mixed overCapMessage/literal conventions in two envoy-client test files) were left alone on the architect's ruling. I re-checked the first myself in round 2: it fails closed, with an ENOENT exit rather than a vacuous pass, and CI never sets the variable.
